findings.title: Rejected devices are cached and allowed on their next request
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` adds the device ID to the local cache before calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When that call returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, this new return rejects the current authentication, but the cache entry remains. A subsequent request from the same new device ID hits the cache and returns success without consulting the store, so `Authenticate` creates an anonymous identity despite the configured limit. Since the cache default TTL is 29 minutes, a device can bypass the limit simply by retrying after its first rejected request. Only cache the ID after a successful store update, or evict it when tagging fails.

findings.title: Count-then-insert does not enforce the limit under concurrent requests
findings.body: The limit check performs `CountDevices` in one database session and then performs the insert/upsert in a separate session. Multiple concurrent requests for distinct device IDs can all observe a count below `deviceLimit` and all insert successfully, exceeding the configured limit. This also occurs across Grafana instances sharing the same database. The check and admission need to be made atomic, for example with a transaction and suitable locking or a database-side conditional/admission mechanism.
